he:Weekday Maariv/Sefirat HaOmer:1.en: After the Amidah in Maariv we begin to count the Omer, which starts on the night of the 16th of Nisan and continues for 49 days. If one forgot to count at the beginning of the night, he counts for the rest of the night. Each person is obligated to count for himself. One must count standing, and bless first. He counts days and weeks: on the first day he stands, blesses "al sefiras ha'omer" and says "Today is one day of the Omer"; and so on until seven days, when he says "Today is seven days, which are one week"; on the eighth day, "eight days, which are one week and one day"; until the fourteenth, "fourteen days, which are two weeks", and so on. Now that the Omer offering is no longer brought, the counting is only rabbinic, in memory of the Temple. If one is in doubt whether he counted, he counts again without a blessing.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:51.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance, conclude:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:53.en: Throughout the year, if one said "HaMelech hamishpat" he has fulfilled his obligation and need not return. During the Ten Days of Repentance, if one mistakenly said "Melech ohev tzedakah umishpat": if he remembers within a moment of speech he says "HaMelech hamishpat"; if later, he does not say it and is not made to repeat.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:64.en: Prayer for Return of Divine Service

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:66.en: On Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed say this:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:74.en: When saying "Modim" one bows the head and body like a reed until the vertebrae loosen. One bows quickly all at once and straightens slowly, head first and then body, so that it is not a burden.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:76.en: On Chanukah and Purim "Al hanissim" is said. If one forgot it and remembered before saying the Name in "HaTov shimcha", even after saying "Baruch Atah" he returns and says "Al hanissim"; but if he already finished the blessing, or said "Baruch Atah Hashem", he does not return.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:83.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:85.en: If one forgot to say "Uchtov": if he remembers before saying the Name in "HaTov shimcha" he returns; if he remembers only after saying the Name he does not return, as explained above regarding "Zochreinu" and "Mi chamocha".

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:89.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:91.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance one says "In the Book of Life". If one did not say it, since he finished the blessing or only said "Baruch Atah", he does not return. It seems that it is proper to say "In the Book" immediately after the one blessing his people Israel with peace, before "Yehi Ratzon", since the prayer is already finished. (Deh"a to R"T: always say at the end of a blessing even for things one doesn't return for, but those who disagree think that since one doesn't need to return, it would be an interruption in the middle of the prayer, which is not the case here.) (Chayei Adam 24:25)

parts.en: He Who makes peace in His high heavens may He make peace upon us and upon all Israel and say Amein.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:97.en: On weekday nights, the Chazzan continues with Whole-Kaddish. On Saturday night, the Chazzan says Half-Kaddish, and the Congregation continues with Vihi No'am and VeAtah Kadosh below. If a Festival occurs on a weekday of the new week, the Chazzan instead says Whole-Kaddish and Vihi No'am/VeAtah Kadosh are omitted. On Purim, the Megillah is read here, followed by (Vihi No'am and) VeAtah Kadosh below. On Tisha B'Av, Eichah and Kinos are said, followed by VeAtah Kadosh.

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:1.en: When night arrives one prays Maariv. It is not an obligation, since it was instituted only to correspond to the limbs and fats of the afternoon Tamid offering that were not consumed by day and continued to burn all night; nevertheless it is a mitzvah and should not be neglected. Rav Alfasi wrote that nowadays it has been established as an obligation and must not be neglected at all.

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:9.en: An individual (praying without a minyan) says:
he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:9.gloss: Said only when there is no minyan

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:12.en: There should be a slight pause between 'echad' and 'Baruch', since the main acceptance of the yoke of Heaven is the first verse. Say the next line quietly.

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:19.gloss: The chazzan repeats the last words of the Shema

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:21.en: "Emet ve'emunah" does not begin with "Baruch", since it is joined to the Shema and so there is no interruption.

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:25.en: One says "Hashkiveinu" and concludes "Shomer amo Yisrael la'ad", because the night needs protection from harmful forces. Although the halachah follows Rabbi Yochanan that one must connect the evening redemption blessing to the Amidah, "Hashkiveinu" is not an interruption, since the Rabbis instituted it as an extension of the redemption.

he:Weekday Maariv/The Shema:27.en: The custom of interrupting with the verses "Baruch Hashem le'olam" and Kaddish dates from when synagogues were in the fields and people feared staying until after nightfall. The verses were instituted with eighteen mentions of the Name, parallel to the eighteen blessings of the Maariv Amidah, and one is released by Kaddish. Although Maariv is now prayed in synagogues, the custom was not abolished, but one should not interrupt with other matters. Some great authorities were accustomed not to say them.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:4.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:6.en: If one forgot to say 'Zochreinu' and remembered after saying 'Baruch Atah' but before the Name, he says 'Zochreinu' and continues 'Melech ozer' in order; if he remembered after the Name he does not return. If one mistakenly says 'Zochreinu' during the rest of the year: if he remembers before saying 'Vechosvenu' he stops and begins 'Melech ozer'; if he said 'Vechosvenu' he returns to the beginning of the prayer.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:14.en: If one erred and did not say 'Mashiv haruach umorid hageshem': if he remembers before saying the blessing 'Mechayeh hameitim' he says it where he remembers; if he remembers only after finishing the blessing he must return to the beginning of the Amidah. If he is unsure whether he said it: after thirty days the presumption is that he prayed correctly; within thirty days he must repeat the prayer.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:16.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:18.en: If one forgot to say 'Mi chamocha av harachamim', the law is the same as for 'Zochreinu'.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:23.en: During the Ten Days of Repentance:

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:25.en: If one mistakenly concluded 'HaEl hakadosh': if he realizes within a moment of speech (about the time to say 'Shalom alecha rebbi') and says 'HaMelech hakadosh' he has fulfilled his obligation; otherwise he must return to the beginning of the Amidah, and likewise if he is unsure whether he said it. During the rest of the year, if he said 'HaMelech hakadosh' he does not return.

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:40.gloss: Sefard/Israel custom; Ashkenaz diaspora omits this line in summer

he:Weekday Maariv/Amidah:45.en: If one forgot to say "Tal umatar" and remembers before beginning "Teka", he says it where he remembers. If he began "Teka", he says it in "Shomea tefilla"; if he did not remember there, he says it between "Shomea tefilla" and "Retzei". If he forgot there too: if he remembers before moving his feet (at the end of the Amidah) he returns to "Bareich aleinu" and continues in order; if he has moved his feet he returns to the beginning of the Amidah.

The three concluding benedictions are known as the benedictions of thanksgiving. They consist of prayers for the re-establishment of God's service at Jerusalem; thanksgiving for God's daily wonders in our behalf; and a prayer for peace and prosperity.
